manifest.name: Osmium Analytics
manifest.description: Cookieless, first-party visitor statistics: visits, top pages, referrers, device and country, with a retention setting

manifest.name: Osmium Blog
manifest.description: Blog posts written in admin and published as ordinary pages under /blog/, with the markup supplied by the theme

manifest.name: Brevo
manifest.description: Send site email through Brevo's HTTP API, and add newsletter signups to a Brevo list. A generous free plan, and useful where hosting blocks outbound SMTP. Appears as a provider on the Email settings page.

setup.postInstallNote: Enter a Brevo API key on the Brevo settings page, and make sure the From address on Settings > Email is a verified sender in Brevo. Then choose Brevo as the Provider on Settings > Email and use Send test email. For newsletter signups, set the List ID on the Brevo settings page, switch signups on, and point the theme form (fields email, consent tick box, token and the zip honeypot) at /api/brevo-newsletter/. The visitor returns with ?newsletter=subscribed, invalid, no_consent or failed. Optional double opt-in: add a confirmation template ID and a thank-you page address, and the result becomes ?newsletter=confirm.

manifest.name: Microsoft Clarity
manifest.description: Microsoft Clarity heatmaps and session recordings - free, consent-gated, gated on an admin-editable toggle and production-only; requires the Cookie Consent service

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. A theme must call ServiceThemeBlocks::render('head', ['site' => $site]) in its <head> template before enabling this does anything visible. Requires Cookie Consent (installed with this service, but disabled by default - enable it too): Clarity gets consent denied until a cookie named osmium_cookie_consent (or window.OsmiumCookieConsent.cookieName) reads 'accepted'. Clarity's own Cookies setting should also be off for no cookies before consent.

manifest.name: Osmium Cookie Consent
manifest.description: GDPR-style cookie consent banner and status ribbon, production-only, with an admin-editable cookie name/privacy URL/colors/copy

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. The 'head' hook (cookie name, Consent Mode wiring for Analytics if also installed, and this service's own site-modal.css and site-modal.js, loaded only when enabled and not on dev/staging) is live-wired into osmium-base's homepage. The 'body-end' hook (banner + status ribbon markup) has no theme calling it yet - a real theme must call ServiceThemeBlocks::render('body-end', ['cookieConsent' => ..., 'site' => $site]) near </body>. A theme no longer loads site-modal.css/js itself.

manifest.name: Osmium FAQs
manifest.description: Named lists of questions and answers managed in admin, for a theme to show anywhere, with FAQPage schema for search engines

setup.postInstallNote: Create a list under Content > FAQs, then show it from a theme controller: $faqs = new \Osmium\Services\Faqs\Models\Faqs($this->osmium->dataSource); $items = $faqs->items('your-slug'); The theme writes the markup; echo \Osmium\Services\Faqs\Models\FaqSchema::script($items) in the page head or body for FAQPage structured data. Each edit page shows the snippet for its own list.

manifest.name: Osmium Featured Products
manifest.description: A hand-picked list of up to 5 featured products, ordered by drag and drop in admin, with an edit lock for busy admin teams and the list handed to the theme

setup.postInstallNote: Pick up to 5 products under Shop > Featured Products. Show them from a theme by including the shop's featured-products controller, which gives the page featuredProducts (product cards in your order). Editing locks the page for other admins until you press Save, or after 30 minutes idle.

manifest.name: FreeAgent
manifest.description: Connects the shop to FreeAgent (OAuth2) and adds a 'Push to FreeAgent' button on paid orders that creates a sales invoice. Locked to one named FreeAgent company

setup.postInstallNote: Pushing is locked until configured. Create an app in the FreeAgent developer dashboard, enter its OAuth identifier/secret on the settings page and add the shown redirect URI to the app. Set Allowed company to the exact name of the FreeAgent company, then connect, then pick the sales category and tax rate. Pushing creates real invoices.

manifest.name: Postcode Geocoder
manifest.description: Looks up a UK postcode's lat/lng via postcodes.io - a pure capability with no admin page of its own, for other services to depend on

manifest.name: Google Analytics
manifest.description: Google Tag Manager / GA4 loading with Consent Mode v2, gated on an admin-editable toggle and production-only; requires the Cookie Consent service

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. A theme must call ServiceThemeBlocks::render('head', ['googleAnalytics' => ..., 'site' => $site]) in its <head> template before enabling this does anything visible.

manifest.name: Google Maps
manifest.description: Draws a map of pins (clustered, with a fullscreen button) on Google Maps, for a theme to place anywhere - the Google counterpart of Leaflet Maps, taking the same pin list. Needs your own API key (billing account); loads Google only after cookie consent

setup.postInstallNote:
Create a Maps JavaScript API key in Google Cloud (billing account required) and restrict it by HTTP referrer to your site. Paste it on the Google Maps settings page and tick Enabled; Cookie Consent must be enabled too. Add once on any page that shows a map, then place a map with
- the same pin JSON as Leaflet Maps: {"pins":[{"lat":51.5,"lng":-0.12,"title":"Name","text":"Details","url":"https://...","inactive":false}],"height":"400px","fullscreen":true}. Install only one of Leaflet Maps and Google Maps on a site. Google loads only after a visitor accepts cookies (on dev and staging, where there is no banner, it loads at once). Untested against a live Google account.

manifest.name: Google Maps Embed
manifest.description: Google Maps Embed (a single place in an iframe) for a theme to place anywhere (e.g. a contact page), from one admin-editable embed URL

setup.postInstallNote: Paste the embed URL on the Google Maps Embed settings page (Google Maps > Share > Embed a map; copy only the src URL, not the whole iframe). Then place the map in a theme with <?php $template['serviceBlock']('map'); ?> where it should appear, e.g. the contact page. Nothing renders until a URL is saved. The iframe loads Google immediately, with no consent step.

manifest.name: Google Merchant Center
manifest.description: Pushes product data to Google Merchant Center (Merchant API) whenever a product is saved, status-changed or removed. Service-account auth, admin-editable credentials, test connection and one-click full sync

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled until configured. Needs a Google Cloud service account added as a user on the Merchant Center account, with its Merchant ID, primary data source ID, and service-account email + private key entered on the settings page. Run 'Test connection', then 'Sync all products' for the initial catalogue push; after that products sync automatically on save.

manifest.name: Google Reviews
manifest.description: Hand-curated Google review admin CRUD and homepage social-proof widget model

manifest.name: hCaptcha
manifest.description: Spam protection for forms via hCaptcha - a privacy-focused alternative to Google reCAPTCHA and Cloudflare Turnstile, admin-editable site/secret key

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. Once enabled with the keys from hCaptcha, every form that fires the form.verify and form.widget hooks (such as the product review form) is protected, with no per-form setup, and the visitor ticks the box before the Submit button works. A theme must echo $template['serviceHeadHtml'] in its <head> so the widget script loads. Other forms can call HcaptchaConfig::verify($_POST['h-captcha-response'] ?? '') directly. Same verify() contract as Turnstile and reCAPTCHA. Install only one protection per form: with several enabled, each shows its widget and all must pass. hCaptcha refuses localhost as a hostname, so test on a hosts-file name.

manifest.name: Leaflet Maps
manifest.description: Draws a map of pins (clustered, with a fullscreen button) from OpenStreetMap tiles using a bundled Leaflet, for a theme to place anywhere - no API key, no cookies

setup.postInstallNote:
Add once on any page that shows a map (it loads Leaflet's CSS and JS). Then place a map with
, where JSON is {"pins":[{"lat":51.5,"lng":-0.12,"title":"Name","text":"Details","url":"https://...","inactive":false}],"height":"400px","fullscreen":true}. title, text, url, inactive, height, fullscreen and consent are optional. Build the JSON with htmlspecialchars(json_encode(...), ENT_QUOTES). Privacy: no cookies are set, but when a map is drawn the visitor's browser fetches tiles from openstreetmap.org, so their IP address reaches OpenStreetMap - name it in your privacy notice. Add "consent":true to a map's JSON to hold it back until the visitor accepts cookies (live sites with Cookie Consent; on dev and staging it draws at once).

manifest.name: Mailgun
manifest.description: Send site email through Mailgun's HTTP API - useful where hosting blocks outbound SMTP. Appears as a provider on the Email settings page.

setup.postInstallNote: Enter the sending domain, region and API key on the Mailgun settings page, then choose Mailgun as the Provider on Settings > Email and use Send test email.

manifest.name: Mailjet
manifest.description: Send site email through Mailjet's HTTP API - a free plan of 6,000 emails a month, and useful where hosting blocks outbound SMTP. Appears as a provider on the Email settings page.

setup.postInstallNote: Enter a Mailjet API key and secret key on the Mailjet settings page, and make sure the From address on Settings > Email is a verified sender or domain in Mailjet. Then choose Mailjet as the Provider on Settings > Email and use Send test email.

manifest.name: Mailtrap
manifest.description: Send site email through Mailtrap - live sending, or a sandbox inbox that catches every email so nothing reaches real customers while testing. Appears as a provider on the Email settings page.

setup.postInstallNote: Enter an API token on the Mailtrap settings page and choose Live sending (a verified sending domain is needed) or Sandbox (enter the inbox ID). Then choose Mailtrap as the Provider on Settings > Email and use Send test email.

manifest.name: Mals Ecommerce
manifest.description: Sells through the Mals hosted cart: add-to-cart buttons post to Mals, the checkout is Mals' own page, and the header shows the cart count. No basket or checkout pages of its own

setup.postInstallNote: Enter the cart user ID and the add-to-cart and checkout URLs from your Mals account under Mals Cart. A theme reads the cart with $mals = \Osmium\Services\Mals\Models\MalsCart::data(); (null when Mals is off or not set up): cartTotalItems, cartID, checkoutLink, addItemLink, hideZeroItems. The add-to-cart form posts to addItemLink with fields userid, product, qty, discountpr (':0,'), units (weight), return, producturl, thumb and nocart. The shop's basket and checkout pages are not used; remove them from the site's pages if the shop switch created them. Prices sent to Mals are ex-VAT. The add-to-cart link inside that form is add to cart: the service loads the script that handles the click (no inline onclick, which the site's security policy blocks), so the theme must print $template['serviceBodyEndHtml'] before .

manifest.name: Meta Pixel
manifest.description: Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Pixel PageView plus optional shop events (ViewContent, AddToCart, Purchase) and server-side Purchase, consent-gated, gated on an admin-editable toggle and production-only; requires the Cookie Consent service

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. A theme must call ServiceThemeBlocks::render('head', ['site' => $site]) in its <head> template before enabling this does anything visible. Requires Cookie Consent (installed with this service, but disabled by default - enable it too): the pixel script is not even fetched from Meta until a cookie named osmium_cookie_consent (or window.OsmiumCookieConsent.cookieName) reads 'accepted'. Shop events and the server Purchase are off until switched on in settings; the theme must output the shop event tags (THEME-CONTRACT.md section 7) and load shop-events.js.

manifest.name: Microsoft 365 Mail
manifest.description: Send site email through the Microsoft Graph API using an Azure AD app registration - for Microsoft 365 tenants that have disabled SMTP AUTH. Appears as a provider on the Email settings page.

setup.postInstallNote: Enter the Tenant ID, Client ID and client secret of an Azure AD app registration with the Mail.Send application permission (admin consent granted) on the Microsoft 365 Mail settings page. Mail is sent as the From address on Settings > Email, so scope the app to that mailbox with an Exchange ApplicationAccessPolicy. Then choose Microsoft 365 Mail as the Provider on Settings > Email and use Send test email.

manifest.name: PayPal
manifest.description: Takes PayPal payments at checkout (Orders v2, server-side capture), with a signature-verified webhook to reconcile orders. Appears as a payment provider in Settings > Payments

setup.postInstallNote: PayPal is off until configured. Enter your client IDs and secrets on the PayPal settings page, create a webhook in the PayPal developer dashboard pointing at /api/checkout-paypal-webhook (events: PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED) and paste its Webhook ID. Then choose PayPal as the Active Checkout Provider in Settings > Payments.

manifest.name: QuickBooks
manifest.description: Connects the shop to QuickBooks (OAuth2) and adds a 'Push to QuickBooks' button on paid orders that creates a sales invoice. Locked to one named QuickBooks company

setup.postInstallNote: Pushing is locked until configured. Create an Intuit developer app (accounting scope), enter its client ID/secret on the settings page and add the shown redirect URI to the app's Redirect URIs. Connect, then set 'Allowed company' to the exact name of the connected QuickBooks company - pushes are refused unless it matches. Pushing creates real invoices. Non-US companies must also set a tax code ID.

manifest.name: Google reCAPTCHA v3
manifest.description: Spam protection for forms via Google reCAPTCHA v3 - score-based, invisible by default, admin-editable site/secret key and score threshold

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. Requires a Google Cloud project with billing enabled and the reCAPTCHA Enterprise/legacy API set up (free tier is 10,000 assessments/month as of April 2026 - see Cloudflare Turnstile instead for an unlimited-free alternative with an identical verify() contract). A theme must call ServiceThemeBlocks::render('head', ['recaptcha' => ..., 'site' => $site]) to load the client script, which auto-executes and writes a token into a hidden #recaptcha-token field on every form (action 'submit'). Every form that fires the form.verify and form.widget hooks (such as the product review form) is protected without per-form setup. A form handler calls RecaptchaConfig::verify($_POST['recaptcha-token'] ?? '') before processing. Install only one protection per form: with several enabled, all must pass.

manifest.name: Resend
manifest.description: Send site email through Resend's HTTP API - a simple developer-friendly API with a free plan, and useful where hosting blocks outbound SMTP. Appears as a provider on the Email settings page.

setup.postInstallNote: Enter a Resend API key on the Resend settings page, and make sure the From address on Settings > Email uses a domain verified in Resend. Then choose Resend as the Provider on Settings > Email and use Send test email.

manifest.name: Osmium Restock Leads
manifest.description: Lets customers leave their email to hear when an out-of-stock product is back, collects those requests, and lists them in admin

setup.postInstallNote: Leads are only collected and listed under Shop > Restock Leads: nothing emails customers when stock returns, so do that yourself. Point the theme's notify-me form (fields email, pid, token and the zip honeypot) at /api/restock-leads/. The product page then gets restockNotifySet (true once this visitor has asked for that product in this session; no cookie of its own is set) and restockNotice (sent or failed, shown once).

manifest.name: Osmium Reviews
manifest.description: Customer product reviews: a submit endpoint with spam protection, moderation in admin, and review data for the product page

setup.postInstallNote: Reviews arrive unpublished: approve them under Shop > Reviews. Point the theme's review form (fields name, email, pid, rating, message, zip honeypot, token) at /api/reviews. The product page then gets reviews, reviewCount, ratingAverage and reviewNotice (sent or failed, shown once). Add the people to email about new reviews under Settings > Reviews.

manifest.name: Sage Accounting
manifest.description: Connects the shop to Sage Accounting (OAuth2) and adds a 'Push to Sage' button on paid orders that creates a sales invoice. Locked to one named Sage business

setup.postInstallNote: Pushing is locked until configured. Create an app in the Sage developer portal, enter its client ID/secret on the settings page and add the shown redirect URI as the app callback URL. Set Allowed business to the exact name of the Sage business, then connect, then pick the sales ledger account and tax rate. Pushing creates real invoices.

manifest.name: Osmium Schema
manifest.description: Site-wide structured data: Organization or LocalBusiness (address, opening hours, contact point, and geo looked up from the postcode) and WebSite, as JSON-LD with fixed @ids other services can reference

setup.postInstallNote: Adds nothing to the page until the site has a name; empty Schema fields fall back to the site name, Branding company details and the uploaded logo. Needs the core change that passes company details to theme blocks. The 'head' hook is output by a theme's <head> template via ServiceThemeBlocks::render('head', [...]). Other services can reference the organisation by its @id: <site URL>/#organization (and <site URL>/#website).

manifest.name: Osmium Search Analytics
manifest.description: Records what customers search for in the shop, shows the top and zero-result searches in admin, and adds a search synonym in one click from a failed search

setup.postInstallNote: Searches are recorded from now on (one row per term per day, no visitor details). Look under Shop > Search Analytics for the top and zero-result searches of the last 30 days, and use Add synonym on a failed search that has a suggestion. Synonyms are saved to the shop's search-synonyms.php, which core search reads whether or not this service is installed.

manifest.name: Osmium Shop
manifest.description: The shop: catalogue, baskets, checkout, orders, discounts and the admin screens that run them

manifest.name: Osmium Shows
manifest.description: Curated trade show/event listings with postcode geocoding and logo upload

setup.postInstallNote: Public listing consumption (e.g. a /shows/ page) isn't included - wire your own page to call the Show model's listUpcoming()/listPast() methods.

manifest.name: Sinch SMS
manifest.description: Send SMS through Sinch's SMS REST API. Admin-editable credentials and sender, plus a test-text button. A capability for core and other services: answers the sms.providers and sms.send hooks

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. Enter the service plan ID, API token, region and a sender (a Sinch number or an alphanumeric sender ID) on the Sinch SMS settings page, press Send test text, then switch on Send SMS through Sinch. This service only sends; core and other services text through the sms.send hook. Only one SMS provider can be installed at a time.

manifest.name: Osmium Social Links
manifest.description: One place for the business's social profile URLs, shown as a list of links by a theme and available to other services such as Schema

setup.postInstallNote: Adds nothing to the page until a link is saved on Content > Social Links. The 'social-links' hook is rendered in place by a theme (for example in its footer) with $template['serviceBlock']('social-links'); the markup is a plain list with a data-network attribute on each item for the theme to style. Icons are opt-in: set an icon class pattern on the settings page, and the theme must load that icon set itself. Other services read the saved URLs from this service's config context as $osmiumSocialLinks['links'] without depending on it.

manifest.name: Square
manifest.description: Takes card payments at checkout through Square (Web Payments SDK card form on your own page, charged server-side with the CreatePayment API). Appears as a payment provider in Settings > Payments

setup.postInstallNote: Square is off until configured. Enter the Application ID, Access Token and Location ID from the Square Developer Console on the Square settings page, then choose Square as the Active Checkout Provider in Settings > Payments. The checkout page's card form must tokenize the card with the Square Web Payments SDK and POST the token to /api/checkout-square-charge before calling the normal order confirmation.

manifest.name: Osmium Stock Control
manifest.description: Counts stock down when an order is paid, stops customers adding more than is in stock, and treats a kit's parts as stock of their own

manifest.name: Stripe
manifest.description: Takes card payments at checkout through Stripe (PaymentIntents, plus Apple Pay/Google Pay via the card element), with a signature-verified webhook to reconcile orders. Appears as a payment provider in Settings > Payments

setup.postInstallNote: Stripe is off until configured. Enter your keys on the Stripe settings page, add a webhook endpoint in the Stripe dashboard pointing at /api/checkout-stripe-webhook (events: payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed, charge.refunded) and paste its signing secret. Then choose Stripe as the Active Checkout Provider in Settings > Payments. Test locally with: stripe listen --forward-to <host>/api/checkout-stripe-webhook

manifest.name: Cloudflare Turnstile
manifest.description: Spam protection for forms via Cloudflare Turnstile - free, no DNS dependency, admin-editable site/secret key and widget mode

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. Once enabled with the keys from Cloudflare, every form that fires the form.verify and form.widget hooks (such as the product review form) is protected, with no per-form setup. The widget loads Cloudflare's script itself, only when the form is near the screen or touched, so pages without a protected form never contact Cloudflare; no theme change is needed. Other forms can call TurnstileConfig::verify($_POST['cf-turnstile-response'] ?? '') directly. The Turnstile settings page shows how many checks passed and failed.

manifest.name: Twilio SMS
manifest.description: Send SMS through Twilio's Messages API. Admin-editable credentials and sender, plus a test-text button. A capability for core and other services: answers the sms.providers and sms.send hooks

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. Enter the Account SID, Auth Token and a sender (a Twilio number, an alphanumeric sender ID, or a Messaging Service SID) on the Twilio SMS settings page, press Send test text, then switch on Send SMS through Twilio. This service only sends; core and other services text through the sms.send hook. Only one SMS provider can be installed at a time.

manifest.name: Vonage SMS
manifest.description: Send SMS through Vonage's SMS API. Admin-editable credentials and sender, plus a test-text button. A capability for core and other services: answers the sms.providers and sms.send hooks

setup.postInstallNote: Disabled by default. Enter the API key, API secret and a sender (a Vonage number or an alphanumeric sender ID) on the Vonage SMS settings page, press Send test text, then switch on Send SMS through Vonage. This service only sends; core and other services text through the sms.send hook. Only one SMS provider can be installed at a time.

manifest.name: Xero
manifest.description: Connects the shop to Xero (OAuth2) and adds a 'Push to Xero' button on paid orders that creates an AUTHORISED sales invoice. Locked to one named Xero organisation

setup.postInstallNote: Pushing is locked until configured. Create a Xero app, enter its client ID/secret on the settings page and add the shown redirect URI to the Xero app. Connect, then set 'Allowed organisation' to the exact name of the connected Xero organisation - pushes are refused unless it matches. Pushing creates real AUTHORISED invoices.
